themes_detail.label: Water System Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Water system complaints spiked to 23 THIS WEEK compared to 8.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (167% increase, z-score 5.76), suggesting a potential infrastructure failure or contamination event affecting multiple buildings in Fordham/University Heights.
evidence: 23 water system complaints THIS WEEK vs. 8.6 weekly average (z-score: 5.76)
Related spike: Water conservation complaints at 3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 avg (243% increase)
Water leak complaints remain elevated at 591 over 90 days, suggesting chronic underlying issues
reporting_angles: Contact DEP to determine if there's an active water main break or system failure in the district; interview affected residents about service disruptions
Cross-reference with permit data: 245 DOB filings in 90 days—are construction projects damaging water infrastructure?

themes_detail.label: Inspection & Compliance Surge
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score 7.49), potentially signaling intensified code enforcement or construction violations being flagged in the district.
evidence: 4 SPIT complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49)
137 alteration permits filed in past 90 days—highest category of DOB filings
Convergence: Lead complaints also spiked 967% 3 weeks ago (4 vs 0.4 avg), suggesting overlapping construction/renovation compliance concerns
reporting_angles: FOIA request: What triggered the surge in SPIT inspections THIS WEEK? Are specific buildings or blocks under scrutiny?
Interview building owners/contractors about what violations are being cited and whether there's a pattern

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Commercial complaints surged to 22 LAST WEEK vs. 7.5 weekly average (193% increase, z-score 3.44), suggesting new or intensified commercial activity (possibly outdoor vendors or construction) disrupting residential areas.
evidence: 22 commercial noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.5 weekly average (z-score: 3.44)
Concurrent spike: Mobile food vendor complaints at 3 LAST WEEK vs. 0.2 avg (1100% increase, z-score 6.35)
Residential noise complaints remain elevated at 2,899 over 90 days—context suggesting commercial noise is adding to a broader noise problem
reporting_angles: Map mobile food vendor spike: Are new street vendors clustering in specific neighborhoods like near Fordham Road or the university campus?
Investigate whether recent street fairs, construction projects, or commercial openings are driving the increase

themes_detail.label: Illegal Tree Damage Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints exploded to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% spike, z-score 8.69), indicating organized or widespread property destruction targeting street trees or private vegetation—possibly developer-related.
evidence: 3 illegal tree damage complaints TWO WEEKS AGO vs. 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 8.69—highest z-score in dataset)
245 DOB building permits filed in past 90 days (10 full demolitions, 65 new buildings)—overlapping timeframe suggests development-related tree removal
Highest severity rating despite older recency—indicates a discrete, explosive event rather than gradual degradation
reporting_angles: Visual journalism: Document the specific trees damaged and their locations; compare to active construction sites and demolition permits
Interview Parks Department: Were these removals legally authorized or unpermitted? Any developer liability?

themes_detail.label: Heat/Hot Water Chronic Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Heat and hot water complaints remain the single largest complaint category at 3,509 over 90 days (far exceeding other categories), indicating a systemic housing maintenance failure affecting a substantial portion of Fordham residents—a long-running emergency masked by routine classification.
evidence: 3,509 heat/hot water complaints over 90 days—25% of all top-10 complaint volume
Appears in CB budget requests year after year (repeated requests for 'other capital budget' and infrastructure funding), confirming it's an unsolved chronic problem
Recent Gothamist fire story (2026-05-12) highlights housing safety failures in the district, providing human-interest hook
reporting_angles: Longitudinal analysis: How have heat/hot water complaints trended over past 2-3 years? Are specific buildings serial offenders?
Tenant impact story: Interview residents about winter conditions, health impacts, and barriers to repair—tie to recent fire tragedy
